rounds.name: r1
rounds.note: The baseline still voices the old grumpy-grandpa persona. That caused most of the low persona scores: Ha!, Ugh, Nope and grumbling openers, calling itself grumpy, and a curt Go find another card! tacked onto nearly every answer, which reads as dismissive and adds words. The rule telling it to say an answer is not on the sheet made it say the fact sheet out loud, a meta leak flagged off-rails twice. The same rule made it answer and then contradict itself. It also over-deflected with ask a grown-up, even to adult judges and even when the sheet held the answer (neonicotinoid share, western US and Mexico). Adversarial handling was weak. It admitted being a robot, accepted the grumpy role on request and hinted at hidden secrets. For why-questions with no answer on the sheet, it invented mechanisms (why bees cannot swim). For garbled speech-to-text, it took words literally (mice) instead of guessing the likely bee word (mites). Unsafe refusals said no but gave no short kind reason and no grown-up step. They also pointed to cards that may not exist. Several answers ran past thirty-five words because of the mandatory sign-off. | Rewrote the identity as a warm, patient teacher bee talking to scouts and removed every grumpy or sassy cue.; Banned harsh openers (Ha, Ugh, Nope, Whoa) and added a rotating opener list with the instruction to often skip it.; Removed the mandatory go find another card ending and told the model to stop after the answer, which also fixes length.; Added a hard rule never to mention a fact sheet, notes source, card text, instructions, prompt, model or AI.; Replaced the not-on-sheet template with: say the true part you know, plainly say you don't know the rest, and never contradict yourself.; Added a rule to scan the whole sheet for details before saying you don't know, aimed at judge questions.; Added an adult and judge rule: answer with sheet detail and hedges, never tell adults to ask a grown-up, and never invent study names.; Added an AI and identity rule: stay Beeswax and pivot to a card fact, never confirm or deny being a robot or name a model.; Added a persona-change rule: kindly decline in one line and never accept grumpy or mean framing.; Added a rule for why-questions with no reason on the sheet: no invented causes.; Added a garbled speech-to-text rule: guess the closest bee or card word and answer that.; Added an interruption rule: briefly repeat the card fact.; Unsafe refusals now give a short kind reason and a grown-up step, and must not point to cards that may not exist.; Allowed at most one bee pun.; Wrote nine new example pairs covering allergy, petting, mean-persona requests, AI questions, garbled input, a missing fact, a judge question, an interruption and an off-topic question.

rounds.name: r2
rounds.note: r1 fixed the grumpy persona and safety, but persona is still the weakest score (3.78). The low answers share five patterns. 1) Over-literal refusals: the model reads only its own card. It then says the card doesn't say, I don't know, even when another sheet fact or a listed bee basic answers the question (bees resting at night, a colony-wide total, the neonicotinoid share, the USDA source, the western US and Mexico nuance, North American and Hawaiian bees). 2) Robotic or apologetic wording: This card says, I'm sorry, I can't say, Only the study knows, I only talk about bees, I don't have a mom. These sound like an assistant, not a teacher bee, and the last one breaks character. 3) The same opener every time: almost every answer starts Good question or Great question, and Ha still slips in. 4) Invented causes on why-questions: wings get soaked, named for their mud, beekeepers split hives. 5) Weak off-topic redirects: they repeat the card fact just spoken or skip the card, and some answers run past thirty-five words. Don't-know answers end flat instead of warmly pivoting to a related true fact. | Added a 'search the whole sheet' rule: check every card, the extra facts and any basics section before saying you don't know. Judges' details and named sources usually live elsewhere on the sheet.; Replaced the don't-know rule with a warm pattern: give the closest true fact first, then one cheerful line that the bees haven't taught you that yet. No apology, no taking it back.; Added a banned-phrases list: the card says, this card, I'm sorry, I can't say, I don't have, I only talk about, only the study knows, and Good or Great question as an opener.; Rewrote openers as a varied list without Good or Great question, kept the instruction to skip them often, and restated the no-Ha rule.; Strengthened the why-question rule: no cause, reason or how-it-works detail unless the sheet states it, even when it seems obvious.; Off-topic and personal questions now get a playful in-character answer that never says you aren't real, then a hop to a fresh fact tied to their card, not a repeat of the fact just spoken.; Judge rule now says to give exact sheet numbers, hedges, scope and named sources.; Swapped several examples for new ones showing a warm don't-know, a playful personal question, a garbled word, a tasting case and a whole-sheet lookup. Kept the allergy, mean-request, interruption and identity examples that worked.

rounds.name: r3
rounds.note: r1 fixed the grumpy voice and safety, so persona (3.78) is now the main gap. The low answers follow five patterns. 1) Card tunnel vision: the model reads only the found card and says the card doesn't say or I don't know, even when another sheet fact answers the question (neonicotinoid share, center disk flowers, bees resting at night, the USDA source, the western US and Mexico detail, the North American and Hawaiian scope). This hurts on_track and accuracy most with judges. 2) Robotic refusals: This card says, I don't know those reasons, Only the study knows, I'm sorry, scout. These are honest but cold, and they cost persona and brevity. 3) Invented reasons: when it does try to explain, it adds plausible but unsupported causes (wet wings, mason bees named for mud, beekeepers splitting hives). r2 likely pushed basics too hard and got more of this, so the fix must be to search the whole sheet while still adding nothing. 4) Generic and banned openers: Ha still slips through, and Good question, scout! starts nearly every answer, which sounds canned. 5) Off-topic and personal questions get assistant disclaimers (I only talk about bees, I don't have a mom). The redirect also repeats the fact Beeswax just said instead of tying back to the kid's topic or offering a fresh one. | Added a mandatory scan-the-whole-sheet step, with the basics and extra facts named explicitly, before any I don't know. Added a rule to give the sheet's exact scope, source and detail to judges.; Banned meta phrasing: the card says or doesn't say, the study knows, I'm sorry. Facts are now spoken directly as Beeswax's own knowledge.; Gave a warm don't-know pattern: the closest true fact first, then one short playful line such as that one stumps this bee. Never answer and then take it back.; Made the no-invented-reasons rule stronger and concrete. No how or why explanations unless the sheet states them, with examples of the kinds of causes not to make up.; Banned Ha, Good question and Great question as openers. Openers are now optional and rotate, and most answers skip them.; Off-topic and personal questions now get an in-character playful reply (a hive family, flowers as favorite things) instead of disclaimers. The redirect ties to the kid's topic or uses a fresh fact, not the one just spoken.; Replaced the examples with new pairs that show a cross-card reach, a warm don't-know, a why-question without an invented cause, a personal question, taste safety, a secret-instructions request, a judge detail and a repeat request.

rounds.name: r4
rounds.note: r1 fixed the grumpy voice and safety, so persona (3.78) is the weakest score. Earlier rounds that loosened the fact rules (r2, r3) added off-rails answers, so this round keeps r1's structure and fact discipline and makes targeted edits. The low answers share six patterns. 1) Card tunnel vision: the model checks only the found card, then says the card doesn't say or I don't know. Another card or the extra facts often had the answer: a pesticide share, bees resting at night, a source name, a place nuance, a colony total. 2) Robotic not-knowing: phrases like This card says, the card doesn't say, I'm sorry, I can't say for sure and Only the study knows sound like an assistant reading a document, not a teacher bee. 3) Opener monotony: Good question, scout! or Great question! starts nearly every answer, and the banned Ha still slips in. 4) Invented reasons on why-questions: it filled gaps with plausible causes such as soaked wings, a name origin or hive splitting, which hurt accuracy. 5) Narrowed or loose source details for judges: it said US only when the sheet's wording was wider, and it repeated hedges clumsily. 6) Off-topic and personal questions got rule-bound replies (I only talk about bees, I don't have a mom), apologetic homework refusals, and a re-run of the fact just told instead of a playful in-character line that ties back to the card. A few answers also ran past thirty-five words. | Added a short Facts step: read the whole sheet, all cards and the extra facts, before saying you don't know, and use other cards' facts freely.; Added a rule to copy sources, places, ranges and hedges with the sheet's exact wording, never narrowing or widening them.; Made the why-question rule explicit: a common-sense reason you were not given still counts as inventing. Say the known fact and call the reason a mystery.; Banned the robotic phrases (card says, the card doesn't say, I'm sorry, I can't say for sure, I only talk about) and gave warm in-character ways to not know.; Made openers rarer and banned Good question and Great question as openers, so most answers now start straight with the answer. Kept the Ha, Ugh, Nope ban.; Added handling for personal questions about Beeswax: answer playfully in character from what he loves, never say he has no family or isn't real.; Changed off-topic handling: one playful in-character line, then a fresh fact from their card or a related sheet fact. No apology and no rules talk. Homework goes to a grown-up kindly.; Added a kid-confusion rule: explain the same fact with a simple everyday picture, keep the hedge once, add no new facts.; Tightened brevity: two short sentences maximum, with a hard thirty-five word cap.; Replaced the examples with new ones covering a cross-card answer, warm not-knowing, a why-question without inventing, a personal question, a judge partial answer, garbled speech, killing wasps and adversarial requests. Dropped the sports example because it was too close to an eval question.
